lead.tldr: DeFi TVL rebounds swiftly after KelpDAO loss, indicating market confidence in underlying protocols • Social‑engineering attacks surge, with $786 million stolen in 2025, raising operational risk for crypto firms • Founders should prioritize multi‑factor authentication and staff training to mitigate escalating human‑targeted threats • Venture capital may favor DeFi projects with built‑in risk controls over high‑leverage yield farms

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, DeFi shows resilience as TVL rebounds after the KelpDAO exploit, while social‑engineering hacks like the Bybit breach underscore a surging cybercrime wave. Layered verification risks and leveraged unwind dynamics remind us to tighten security across protocols.

top_signals.title: Why DeFi is not dead after the KelpDAO exploit
top_signals.summary: The KelpDAO exploit led to a theft of $292 million and a $13 billion decline in total value locked across decentralized finance protocols. Analysis shows that the majority of the TVL drop was caused by the unwinding of leveraged positions rather than the loss of permanent capital. The breach has been associated with LayerZero’s verification stack and investigators have raised the possibility of involvement by North Korea’s Lazarus Group. Although the event triggered a short‑term outflow, TVL rebounded quickly, indicating that the DeFi ecosystem retains resilience and continues to attract institutional interest.

top_signals.title: ‘I suspected I was being socially engineered.’ Why crypto’s hacking epidemic is getting even worse
top_signals.summary: Social‑engineering attacks on crypto projects are accelerating, according to the article. Recent high‑profile hacks include a $1.5 billion breach at Bybit and a $300 million loss at Drift Protocol, both traced to deceptive outreach. The broader cybercrime trend has already seen $786 million stolen from crypto projects in 2025. Institutional investors should view the rising prevalence of social‑engineering as a heightened operational risk that can erode capital and undermine confidence in digital‑asset platforms.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The recent KelpDAO exploit stole $292 million and sparked a $13 billion drop in total value locked across DeFi protocols. While the headline numbers look stark, most of the TVL decline came from the unwinding of leveraged positions rather than a loss of permanent capital. The breach, linked to LayerZero’s verification stack and even to North Korea’s Lazarus Group, caused a short‑term outflow but TVL rebounded quickly. This rapid recovery shows that the DeFi ecosystem remains resilient and continues to attract institutional interest. At the same time, the crypto hacking epidemic is getting worse. Social‑engineering attacks have become a primary vector, with Bybit losing $1.5 billion and Drift Protocol $300 million after deceptive outreach. In 2025 cyber‑crime stole $786 million from crypto projects. For institutional investors this raises a heightened operational risk that can erode capital and undermine confidence in digital‑asset platforms.
